body.statement: For every \(r\in(0,1)\), \(w\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta>0\), the equation \((1-w)(\theta-1)m_0^2+[1+(w-r)(\theta-1)]m_0-r=0\) has exactly one feasible root \(m_0\in(0,1)\), namely \(m_0=\kappa(r,w,\theta)\); with \(m_1=\theta m_0/\{1+(\theta-1)m_0\}\), it uniquely solves \(r=(1-w)m_0+wm_1\).
body.justification: This isolates the unique legal branch and prevents denominator-clearing artifacts from entering the global program.
body.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin derive the corresponding fixed-parameter positive root; the present lemma records the probability-scale root including removable and boundary cases needed by an exact optimizer.
body.consumer: The endpoint certificate uses this root to reject every algebraic candidate that lies on the wrong mixture branch.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(r\in(0,1)\), \(w\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta>0\).  Put
\[
T_\theta(z)=\frac{\theta z}{1+(\theta-1)z},\qquad
f_\theta(z)=(1-w)z+wT_\theta(z),\qquad 0\leq z\leq1.
\]
The denominator in \(T_\theta\) is \(1-z+\theta z>0\), and
\[
T_\theta'(z)=\frac{\theta}{\{1+(\theta-1)z\}^2}>0,\qquad
f_\theta'(z)=(1-w)+wT_\theta'(z)>0.
\]
Moreover, \(f_\theta(0)=0\) and \(f_\theta(1)=1\).  The intermediate-value theorem and strict monotonicity therefore give exactly one \(m_0\in(0,1)\) such that \(f_\theta(m_0)=r\), and then \(m_1=T_\theta(m_0)\in(0,1)\) is unique.

Multiplication by the strictly positive denominator \(1+(\theta-1)m_0\) gives, without introducing an extraneous solution,
\[
(1-w)(\theta-1)m_0^2+\bigl[1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\bigr]m_0-r=0.
\]
Write \(B=1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\) and \(D=B^2+4(1-w)(\theta-1)r\).  If \(\theta=1\), the displayed equation is \(m_0-r=0\).  If \(\theta\neq1\), the unique feasible root, including the linear case \(w=1\), is
\[
m_0=\frac{2r}{B+\sqrt D}.
\]
Indeed, when \(w<1\) this is the quadratic root obtained by rationalizing \((-B+\sqrt D)/\{2(1-w)(\theta-1)\}\), and uniqueness of the root in \((0,1)\) selects its nonnegative square root.  Its denominator is positive: for \(\theta>1\) and \(w<1\), \(D>B^2\); for \(\theta<1\), \(B=1-(w-r)(1-\theta)>0\); and for \(w=1\), \(B=r+(1-r)\theta>0\) and \(D=B^2\).  Thus this root is exactly \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mixture\text{-}root}\), including its removable value at \(\theta=1\), and the claimed mixture identity follows from \(f_\theta(m_0)=r\).
